Job Description
Design the analog technology at the heart of advanced infrared imaging systems.
As a Senior Analog Engineer, you’ll take a leading role in the development of infrared image sensor arrays, with ownership spanning analog IC design, ROIC architecture, performance analysis, simulation, integration, and validation .
You’ll influence chip-level architecture, evaluate critical design tradeoffs, and develop analog signal paths and timing architectures that directly impact image performance. This is a hands-on technical role that combines system-level analysis with detailed transistor-level design and simulation.
You’ll also provide technical leadership to digital and layout engineers, collaborate with Test and Systems Engineering through product characterization, and interface with customers on requirements and technical performance.
This role offers the opportunity to expand your technical ownership and grow toward a Principal Analog Designer position.
What You’ll Do
- Lead analog design activities for infrared image sensor arrays and Read-Out Integrated Circuits (ROICs).
- Translate customer and system requirements into IC architecture, analog circuitry, timing, and performance requirements.
- Develop analog IC blocks, signal paths, floor plans, and timing architectures.
- Perform transistor-level and SPICE simulations, including noise, power, variability, small-signal, and performance analysis.
- Conduct design trade studies and contribute to chip-level architectural decisions.
- Evaluate layout parasitics and their impact on circuit performance.
- Work with foundry PDKs and support foundry interactions and IC tape-out.
- Provide technical direction and coordination to digital designers, layout engineers, and other members of the design team.
- Partner with Test and Systems Engineering to support IC characterization, verification, and hardware debugging.
- Create clear technical documentation and present designs, performance analysis, and tradeoffs to engineering teams and customers.
Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline. Master’s degree or PhD preferred.
- Relevant professional experience may be considered in lieu of education.
- 8+ years of experience in analog or mixed-signal IC design or a closely related field.
- Strong experience with analog CMOS design, circuit topology, and schematic capture.
- Experience with ROICs, image sensor electronics, or related IC architectures.
- Strong knowledge of SPICE simulation, noise analysis, small-signal analysis, and circuit performance.
- Experience analyzing layout parasitic effects.
- Experience working with foundry PDKs and supporting the IC tape-out process.
- Experience with IC characterization, testing, or hardware debugging.
- Ability to provide technical leadership and collaborate across IC Design, Layout, Systems, and Test Engineering.
- Strong technical communication and presentation skills.
- Must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident.
Preferred Experience

- Infrared imaging systems
- ROIC or image sensor design
- Electro-optical systems
- Mixed-signal IC design
- Advanced analog CMOS design
- Foundry interaction and process technologies
- IC characterization and test
- Technical leadership of multidisciplinary design teams
- Customer-facing technical design reviews

- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Health, dental, vision, and life insurance starting Day 1
- Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays
- 401(k) with company match
- Employee Stock Purchase Plan
- Educational tuition reimbursement
- Career growth and development opportunities
- Collaborative, highly technical engineering environment
- Fun employee events throughout the year

jobs.description:
About the role
Design high-efficiency Class D power output stages for automotive and consumer audio amplifier products. You will own the switching power path from architecture through silicon validation, including gate drivers, H-bridge and BTL output stages, dead-time control, and protection circuits in high-volume production ICs. Products include both monolithic power stages and multi-chip module GaN based solutions.
Responsibilities
- Architect and design Class D power output stages: H-bridge and BTL configurations, gate drivers, charge pumps, level shifters, dead-time control, and shoot-through protection
- Design high-voltage switching circuits with focus on efficiency, thermal performance, and EMI compliance
- Develop transistor-level schematics in Cadence Virtuoso and verify performance across PVT corners using SPICE simulation
- Collaborate with systems, layout, and applications engineers to meet audio performance specifications (THD+N, IMD, SNR, PSRR, idle channel noise) and power delivery targets
- Analyze and resolve design issues from prototype through production qualification, including EMI/EMC characterization and LC filter optimization
- Contribute to IP reuse strategy and design methodology improvements
- Mentor junior engineers on analog design fundamentals, simulation best practices, and design-for-manufacturing techniques
- Provide technical leadership within the design team: guide design reviews, drive architecture decisions, and establish standards for schematic quality and documentation
Change the world. Love your job.
Designers bring semiconductors to life by defining, developing and/or modifying analog and mixed signal electronic parts, components, or integrated circuitry. They work with other designers and the broader R&D and demand creation teams to align on approaches and parameters for a given device, creating block level specifications for the designs. They take the designs through the concept, implementation in schematic and supervising layout, followed by tape out to the fab. They also support silicon validation, test, qualification for reliability, and finally ramp to mass production. Designers also conduct tests and analyze data to ensure the chosen methods are optimal for the defined specifications and reliability requirements.

jobs.description:
We can't predict what the future holds, but we know Texas Instruments will have a part in shaping it.
Kilby Labs is the advanced R&D and product development support organization within TI chartered to define and develop new and innovative technologies and solutions in collaboration with business units and customers.
As a member of Kilby Labs you’ll have the chance to interact with many product groups and functions, work with an interdisciplinary team, bridge from lab to fab to develop technologies, enable new markets, and scale-up for volume products.
About the Position
Kilby Labs is seeking a highly motivated Silicon Photonics Design Engineer to design silicon photonics solutions for advanced data communications applications and establish methodologies, tools, and automation flows for silicon photonics design. In this role, you will be responsible for the design and layout of transmit and receive Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs). The role includes working closely with system architecture, packaging, validation, and test engineering team members to ensure successful prototyping, product development, and launch. The role requires a creative problem-solver with a strong background in electromagnetic design fundamentals who can develop unique, breakthrough technologies that leap-frog the state-of-the-art and contribute across various aspects of a project.
Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to :
- Design and develop passive and active PIC components such as advanced passive waveguide circuit elements, and high-speed active components such as modulators and Ge-based waveguide detectors for high performance (>200Gbps/ln) datacom applications, while driving continuous improvements in power efficiency and area.
- Work closely with systems and design team members to understand system specifications and translate them into circuit level requirements.
- Collaborate with layout team to translate the designs into DRC clean layouts that meet specifications while guaranteeing high yields.
- Engage with systems and packaging teams to architect, design and simulate advanced packaging solutions for high bandwidth and high-density interfaces for datacom applications.
- Drive test methodology and collaborate with characterization and product engineering teams to enable product validation and production ramp.
- Collaborate with technology development team to define process requirements and specifications for new silicon photonics platforms.
- Participate in R&D to develop next generation photonics technologies, drive IP development.
- Present work and findings to internal and external stakeholders through technical documents and design reviews.
Minimum Requirements :
- Master’s or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Applied Physics, Photonics, Optical Communications or related field.
- Experience with high-speed modulator and detector design and/or passive photonic component design and photonic integrated circuit design.
- Strong understanding of PIC circuit design and layout, experience contributing to or leading PIC tapeouts.
- Experience with electromagnetic and photonic simulators such as HFSS, Lumerical, Tidy3D, PhotonDesign, Optiwave, COMSOL.
- Proficiency with IC design tools (Cadence Virtuoso, Maestro, LayoutXL) as well as photonic design enablement tools such as Synopsys, Luceda, GDSFactory.
- Ability to work both independently and as part of a team, with strong verbal and written communication skills.
- Ideal candidate must excel at promoting new ideas, building collaborative relationships and working across organizations to work on common goals.
Preferred Qualifications :
- Experience with Electronic-Photonic Design Automation (EPDA) flows, co-simulating photonic circuits with CMOS driver/TIA circuits in a unified environment.
- Experience using scripted layout frameworks to automate complex photonic routing.
- Experience with package and board design tools such as Synopsys Altium and Cadence Allegro.
- Experience with hands-on silicon photonics volume test and wafer-level test automation
- Experience with technical approaches for next-gen (beyond 200 Gb/s/lane) silicon photonics including non-silicon materials

jobs.description:
Change the world. Love your job.
TI is seeking an innovative and highly skilled GaN Device Project Lead Engineer to join our cutting-edge Gallium Nitride (GaN) Technology Development Team. This role offers the unique opportunity to work at the forefront of developing Gallium Nitride technology that is redefining the power electronics landscape — enabling higher efficiency, faster switching, and smaller, more reliable systems. You will be instrumental in developing and scaling GaN power process technologies for high-volume manufacturing. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to deliver state-of-the-art devices with world-class performance and reliability.
About the job
This position is focused on leading the development, characterization and optimization of gallium nitride (GaN) power devices. As part of TI's Advanced Technology Development (ATD) team, the role involves close collaboration with fab/manufacturing, business units and Kilby Labs. This position requires in-depth knowledge of III-nitride materials, device physics, and reliability. The scope of the job includes, but not limited to:
- GaN device simulations (TCAD), device design, layout
- Develop robust process flows, drive design-of-experiment (DOE) execution, and solve complex integration challenges
- Collaboration with fab/manufacturing engineers to ensure device manufacturability
- Collaboration with reliability engineers to meet device reliability requirements
- Failure root-cause investigation for device/process/reliability/yield improvement

- Power FETs and other relevant semiconductor device physics

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills are a must as the position requires interfacing with multiple teams

- Proven ability to work across functional teams and drive results in a fast-paced R&D environment
